rounds.fact: Ticketmaster moved a huge chunk of its ticket sales online in the late 90s, a shift that eventually made its service fees a much more visible (and criticized) part of buying tickets.
Suck.com pioneered a sarcastic, link-heavy, first-person writing style that influenced blog voice for years, despite the site itself shutting down back in 2001.
The Wall was a single editable text field in the earliest versions. 2007's platform launch brought app chaos, sheep-throwing included, before the News Feed took over the world.
LinkedIn launched in 2003 out of a founder's living room. By 2005 it was already leaning into the dense, spreadsheet-like profile layout that professional networking sites still use.
Barnes & Noble launched bn.com in 1997 specifically to compete with Amazon, one of the first major traditional retailers to take online bookselling seriously.
